culture.howto_title: How to Use the Culture Guide
culture.howto_text: In every quarterly 1-on-1 and annual review, score each staff member on all four values using a 1-5 scale. Right Person lives these values naturally. Right Seat is separate - both matter.

values.name: Humble
values.description: Humility is the foundation. Not thinking less of yourself - thinking of yourself less. We take Jesus seriously and not ourselves.
behaviors: Gives credit freely; takes blame personally
Asks for help without ego; actively seeks feedback
Serves outside their job description without complaint
Deflects praise toward the team and toward God
Listens more than they talk; curious, not defensive
Does not hoard information, decisions, or control

values.name: Hungry
values.description: Hungry people are self-motivated. They pursue excellence because they love Jesus and love the mission.
behaviors: Pursues personal spiritual formation proactively
Reads, learns, and brings new ideas without being asked
Sets goals beyond what is required; moves the ball
Champions improvement and resists we have always done it this way
Takes on extra responsibility when the mission requires it
Execution-oriented - follows through without reminders

values.name: Happy
values.description: Happy means we know who we are in Christ, why we are here, and find genuine joy in the work - even the hard parts.
behaviors: Brings energy to the team, not drama
Practices personal disciplines that sustain health (Sabbath, prayer, margin)
Celebrates wins - big and small - genuinely and publicly
Treats volunteers and guests with consistent warmth
Does not complain without offering a solution
Can receive hard feedback without falling apart

values.name: Honest
values.description: We say hard things with grace. No triangulating, no gossip, no sweeping things under the rug.
behaviors: Says what they mean in the room, not after the meeting
Admits mistakes quickly and owns outcomes fully
Brings problems forward - not sideways or backwards
Addresses conflict directly with the person involved
Keeps confidences; never leaks private matters
Does not shade truth to protect comfort or avoid awkwardness

ids.title: Rocks List and IDS Process
ids.description: IDS - Identify, Discuss, Solve - is how you actually fix problems instead of talking around them forever. The Issues List is the shared, visible list of everything getting in the way.
ids.rule_text: Whoever identifies an issue owns putting it on the list - not solving it alone. The team solves it together in the L10. Issues are prioritized by impact, not urgency. An issue that recurs 3x becomes a Rock to fix systemically.

steps.label: Identify
steps.text: State the real issue, not the symptom. Sundays feel rushed means the issue is no documented run-of-show assigned. Be specific.

steps.label: Discuss
steps.text: Open the floor until the root issue is truly clear. Do not jump to solutions. Time-boxed to 15 min/issue.

steps.label: Solve
steps.text: Create one To-Do: one owner, one due date. Issue is resolved or removed. Done.

culture_notes: Name personnel and pastoral issues clearly. Calling it tension does not solve it.
Issues belong to the team, not the person who raised them. No retaliation culture.
Never escalate to Ryan what Brad can solve. Never escalate to Brad what a director can solve.
IDS is not a venting session. Time-box discussion.
The Stepping Stones transition (post-Feb 2025) created systemic issues - these are boulders, not just IDS items.
The Wonder gap means issues may not surface until critical. Build in What are we missing? as a standing L10 prompt.
escalation: Issue appears in IDS for the 1st time - To-Do with owner + due date
Issue reappears for 2nd time - escalate priority; examine root cause
Issue appears for 3rd time - becomes a company Rock next quarter
Issues involving Right Person / Right Seat - always escalate to Brad for private 1-on-1
Building / facility issues - Ryan + Brad own together; surface at every QOM

tlhTemplates.label: Recruiting a New Volunteer
tlhTemplates.text: Hey [Name]! I've been thinking about you and wanted to reach out. We have a spot on the [Team Name] team at Living Stones that I think would be a perfect fit for you. It's a great group of people and a really meaningful way to get plugged in. Would you be open to chatting about it this Sunday? No pressure at all — just wanted to plant the seed! 😊

tlhTemplates.label: Schedule Reminder (Pre-Sunday)
tlhTemplates.text: Hey team! 👋 Just a reminder that we're serving together this Sunday. Please plan to arrive by [arrival time] and head to [location]. Looking forward to seeing you all! Let me know if anything has come up. — [Your name]

tlhTemplates.label: Missed Sunday Follow-Up
tlhTemplates.text: Hey [Name] — missed you on Sunday! Just wanted to check in and make sure everything is okay. Life happens and we totally get it. If something's going on or you need to talk through your schedule, I'm here. Hope to see you soon! — [Your name]

tlhTemplates.label: Welcome to the Team
tlhTemplates.text: Hey [Name]! 🎉 So glad you're officially on the [Team Name] team! Here's what to know: we communicate through [communication method], schedules come through Planning Center (check your email for the invite), and your first Sunday you'll shadow [mentor name]. Don't hesitate to text me any time. Can't wait to serve with you! — [Your name]

tlhTemplates.label: Volunteer Appreciation
tlhTemplates.text: Hey [Name] — I just wanted to take a second to say thank you. What you do every week on the [Team Name] team makes a real difference, and I don't always say that enough. You show up, you give your best, and people's experience at Living Stones is genuinely better because of you. Grateful for you! — [Your name]

tlhTemplates.label: Asking for a Sub / Coverage
tlhTemplates.text: Hey team — we're a little short this Sunday for [service/time]. Would anyone be able to step in or swap another week for someone who couldn't make it? You'd be a huge help. Reply here or text me directly. Thanks! — [Your name]
